text:
jordan (customer): Hey support — after switching our PSC consumer forwarding-rule to use the new service attachment in project-redwood-prod (us-central1) our gRPC calls to inference.redwood.example.com are failing with 503 / UNAVAILABLE. Seen since 10:23 UTC. Trace id: trace-8f3a

meera (support): Sorry for the trouble. Are you using Private Service Connect (PSC) forwarding rules to an internal regional ILB, or PSC consumer-facing forwarding rule? Also can you share `gcloud compute forwarding-rules describe` output for the address?

jordan (customer): We're using PSC consumer forwarding rules created via gcloud in us-central1. Forwarding rule points to address 10.200.5.12 (reserved). Here's the describe:
```
name: fw-psc-inference
IPAddress: 10.200.5.12
region: us-central1
target: SERVICE_ATTACHMENT:projects/redwood-prod/.../serviceAttachments/sa-inference
```

alex (infra): quick question: when you moved the forwarding rule, did the consumer project accept the service attachment? If not PSC will NACK and ILB healthchecks will fail, causing 503s.

jordan (customer): Yes it was accepted: `gcloud compute service-attachments list --consumer-project=prd-cust` shows accepted.

ryan (sre): Looking at our logs, the ILB healthchecks for that SA are receiving probes from us-east1 ranges and being blocked by the customer's VPC egress firewall (deny default). Jordan, can you paste `gcloud compute health-checks describe` and any VPC firewall rules that might deny 130.211.0.0/22 or 35.191.0.0/16? GCP ILB health checks come from those ranges.

jordan (customer): Ah — our egress allowlist only had ports to 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 but we do have a deny for "ingress from unknown GCP health ranges". Here's firewall rule: `deny tcp 130.211.0.0/22,35.191.0.0/16` (legacy rule). Removing that allowed the probes.

meera (support): Another thing: DNS TTL. If your app cached the A record pointing to the old regional IP (us-east1) and we introduced new IP in us-central1, some hosts may keep hairpinned routes. Try flushing node-level DNS cache or lowering TTL next cutovers.

jordan (customer): After removing the deny and flushing DNS on pods (kubectl rollout restart), errors dropped to zero. Confirmed gRPC now returns 200 and TLS handshake uses SNI `inference.redwood.example.com` and certs look good. Thanks :tada: 

meera (support): Great. For posterity, checklist we recommend:
- Ensure service attachment accepted
- Allow ILB healthcheck CIDRs (130.211.0.0/22, 35.191.0.0/16)
- Verify forwarding-rule reserved IP matches region of service attachment
- Flush DNS TTLs or use short TTL during cutover
- Check egress/NAT rules for healthcheck source ranges

jordan (customer): Will do. One oddity: the customer's kube-proxy conntrack held stale connections for ~60s which caused some initial 5xx spikes; rolling pods cleared it.

ryan (sre): Noted. We'll add this case to support runbook. deploy-bot: please create ticket.

deploy-bot: Created INC-2026:psc-healthcheck-egress-firewall

jordan (customer): Thanks everyone, good to close.
